method: 200k uniform odd starts in [10^6, 10^9], compute â^(n)(N) tuple, bin by tuple, compute TV vs Geom(2)^n. Fit log_2(TV) vs n.
interpretation: TV is increasing, not decreasing. This contradicts Tao Prop 1.9's qualitative form but is an artifact of the experimental setup, not a real result.

two_artifacts_explaining_growth.name: alphabet_explosion
two_artifacts_explaining_growth.explanation: Number of distinct â tuples grows as ~3^n. With 200k samples, by n=8 we have 76k distinct tuples, ~2.6 samples per tuple. Sampling noise floor scales as sqrt(K)/sqrt(N) where K=alphabet size, so noise ~ 3^(n/2)/sqrt(N). For n=8, N=200k: noise ~ 0.04. Observed TV: 0.34 (8x noise floor, suggesting some real signal but mostly sampling artifact).

two_artifacts_explaining_growth.name: wrong_sampling_distribution
two_artifacts_explaining_growth.explanation: Tao Prop 1.9 hypothesis requires N approximately uniform mod 2^(n') for n' >= (2+c_0)n. Uniform on [10^6, 10^9] is approximately uniform mod 2^k only for k <= 20. For n=8, n' ~ 32 needed but our range covers only mod 2^30. Logarithmic sampling on [y, y^alpha] as in Tao is not used here.

recommended_replacement_task: Subsample 1M-orbit cache with logarithmic weights, compute TV at n=1..6 with validity check N_samples/3^n > 100. See task phi in conversation.
headline: Calibration artifact: this test does NOT verify Tao's exponential TV decay because (a) sample size insufficient at n>=4 and (b) sampling distribution wrong. Tao's bound remains untested empirically; recommended task above provides correct method.
